source_evidence: Point-to-point. This method compares the index level at two points in time, such as the beginning and ending dates of the time period. Averaging. This method compares an average of the index levels at periodic intervals during the time period to the index level at the beginning of the time period.
question: How do point-to-point and averaging methods differ when calculating an indexed annuity’s return?
answer: Point-to-point compares the index level at two times, such as the start and end of the period. Averaging compares the index level at the start with an average of index levels observed at intervals during the period.
